Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday (November 28) said Karnataka would organise a ‘Delhi Chalo’ protest after the Assembly session in December if the Centre failed to release drought relief funds before the session concluded.
He said the State had not received any financial assistance from the Union government for drought relief and that no announcement had been made on the matter.
Also Read: Drought report: On southwest monsoon, drought in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
“Even today, the Central government has not given a single rupee, nor has it announced anything,” he said, pointing out that Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara had furnished the necessary details at a special Cabinet meeting.
The Chief Minister said the State would continue its efforts to secure assistance and would approach the Supreme Court. He had also sought an appointment with the Prime Minister for an all-party delegation to explain the drought situation and the State’s requirements.
“We will go to the Supreme Court and we will go to Delhi. I have also requested the Prime Minister to give us time for an all-party delegation,” he said.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said he was in discussions with the Chief Ministers of Telangana and Kerala, among others, on what he described as the potential impact of delimitation on Karnataka and other southern States.
He said the discussions centred on the possible consequences of population-based changes in representation and the need to protect the interests of southern States.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Cabinet clears Delimitation Bill: 50% seat hike across states, special sitting Nov 30
He had earlier participated in a meeting convened by the DMK in Chennai and said another meeting involving political parties was scheduled in Delhi. The parties would discuss the implications of the proposed changes before deciding their position, he said.
“All parties have agreed to women’s reservation. But the issue of increasing the number of seats needs discussion. We will announce our party’s stand after the meeting,” he said.
He criticised the BJP’s approach, alleging that it was guided by its political interests, and said southern States would have to work together to safeguard their interests.
